After selecting characters, your cowboys are placed on action track locations that allow you to construct buildings, houses, or roads; claim ground; earn money; or score victory points. When more than one player is on the same location, get ready, it is time for a duel! Roll the dice and see if you are the last one standing and lay claim to the goods! During the game, you can take various actions that earn you victory points for your plots, pistols (the hired help), and buildings. At the end of the game, your buildings, houses, mountains, and money contribute to your victory points, and the person with the most points wins. So go round up your posse of gunslingers and get ready for some Wild West action in Carson City! Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 How To Play 1.1 Phase 1 - Choose Characters 1.2 Phase 2 - Place Cowboys 1.3 Phase 3 - Resolve Actions 1.4 Phase 4 - Clean Up 2 Duels 3 Actions 4 Buildings & Income 5 End of Game How To Play The game plays over 4 rounds and each round is divided into 4 phases. The game primarily scores through collecting or buying points as an action. Phase 1 - Choose Characters Choose Characters in passing order (random on first turn) and get the character bonus. This decides the new turn order based on the chosen character's number. Phase 2 - Place Cowboys Place your cowboys on actions in turn order until all players have passed, actions will be resolved in snake order. If you place on a spot with another player a duel will occur in the next phase. Phase 3 - Resolve Actions Resolve actions following the snake from 1-16; if two or more players are on the same spot a duel occurs. Phase 4 - Clean Up Building will move down the snake becoming cheaper and new ones added. Duels If several cowboys are on the same action or parcel of land a duel will occur, unless marked with an X through the Revolver icon. The player with the highest strength will win. Strength = Die Roll + Revolver Icons (on tokens, and characters) + Cowboys in your supply Ties are broken by the person furthest left on the passing track. Losing cowboys are merely injured instead of killed and returned to the players supply. Actions Eagle Valley Arms Wages - Get $4 or buy a horse for $4. no duels. Ammunition - Get 3 extra revolvers this round. The Virginia & Truckee Roads 1 - Get 3 road tokens. Roads 2 - Get 1 road token. no duels. Parcel Purchase To buy a new parcel of land you place your cowboy in that square. You may only buy parcels that no other players already own. You may buy a parcel with a house or a mountain on it. You must pay $1 plus $1 for each building, mountain or house in or adjacent to it. George Alexander Construction Building Purchase - Pay $ printed under the building and place the building on an empty property tile or save the building for later. Deferred Placement - Place your saved buildings on empty property tiles Nevada State Bank Parcel Income - Get $2 per property tile you own. Cowboy Income - Get $2 per revolver and cowboy in your personal supply. Gambling Income - Roll 2 dice and get the result in $. Building Income - Get $ from your buildings and resolve attacks on buildings.1 Town Council of Carson City Parcel VP - Get 1 point for each pair of parcels. Cowboy VP - Get 1 point for each pair of revolvers and cowboys in your personal supply. Building VP - Get 1 point for each of your buildings placed on the board. VP Purchase - Buy 1 point for either $5, $4, $3 or $2 each. Round End Spend money that is beyond your characters cash limit spending $10 each point. Receive new cowboys. Cowboys are not placed on 5, 7 or 11. Buildings & Income Some buildings give you more $ depending on what is adjacent to it and if you own other buildings. [Rating: 3/10] Everything I hate in a euro in one box.   Wedgie tight (~ 17 total worker actions per game). Take-that interaction (workers can knock you off if they have more guns, part of which is a die roll). Random dice rolling.  The role selection is magnificent, and the city building is cool. Without those this game would be a 1 for me.  #BanList
